statement: Whenever sort_linked_list head returns Result.ok r, let ys be the sequence of values of the nodes of r from front to back. Then ys is non-decreasing (for every i with 0 <= i < len(ys)-1, ys[i] <= ys[i+1]) and has the same multiset as xs (for every integer v, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(ys) and ys[i] = v equals the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(xs) and xs[i] = v). Equivalently, ys is the unique non-decreasing rearrangement of xs.
preconditions: Let xs be the sequence of values of the nodes of head from front to back. The preconditions are: 1 <= len(xs) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(xs), -5000 <= xs[i] <= 5000; and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(xs), |xs[i]| <= |xs[j]|, where |v| is the usual absolute value (v if v >= 0, -v otherwise).

Define neg(xs) to be the sequence of those xs[i] with xs[i] < 0, taken in increasing index order, and define neg(ys) similarly from ys. Then neg(ys) is the reverse of neg(xs): len(neg(ys)) = len(neg(xs)) and for every k with 0 <= k < len(neg(xs)), neg(ys)[k] = neg(xs)[len(neg(xs))-1-k].
